24238.title: Sketcher: Trim does not work with an external line and a circle
24238.feasibility_reason: The issue is confirmed and described with a sample file and screenshots, making it reproducible. However, debugging geometric trim algorithms in FreeCAD's Sketcher workbench involving external geometry (reference geometry) requires understanding OCC and Sketcher intersection logic.
24238.problem_summary: Sketcher's trim tool removes an entire circle instead of cutting it at intersections with external geometry lines.
24238.root_cause_hypothesis: The intersection calculation logic in the Sketcher trim command only considers normal/internal sketch geometry (positive geometry indices) and ignores or skips external geometry elements (stored separately or indexed with negative IDs), causing the trim algorithm to detect zero intersection points and delete the entire circle.
24238.suggested_approach: Include external geometry curves when finding intersections for the curve being trimmed, ensuring intersection points can be computed with projected external lines/curves while ensuring the external geometry itself remains unmodified.
prerequisites: Local FreeCAD build environment with Sketcher module enabled
Understanding of SketchObject internal vs. external geometry representations and GeoEnum indexing
implementation_steps: Inspect the trim tool implementation (search for `trim` methods in `SketchObject` and `CommandSketcherTools`) to locate where intersection points with candidate cutting geometries are computed.

Examine how candidate intersecting curves are collected: determine whether the iteration is restricted to `sketch->getGeometry()` without considering `sketch->getExternalGeometry()` / negative indices.
Update the intersection gathering logic to also include external geometries (or projected curves of external geometry) as potential cutting entities.
Ensure intersection points against bounded external geometry (e.g., line segments) properly check parameter bounds / tolerance.

Handle constraint creation or endpoint positioning when splitting a circle into an arc so that point-on-object or coincidence constraints with the external geometry work properly if auto-constraints are enabled.
Verify that trimming an external curve directly is still disallowed or prevented, and only normal geometries are modified/trimmed.
Add automated or manual regression tests verifying trimming circles, arcs, and lines against external geometry lines and curves.

19709.title: Measurement: Error when clicking on measure label only on DXF import
19709.feasibility_reason: The issue provides clear reproduction steps and a stack trace indicating a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when clicking a measure label on a DXF import. However, debugging GUI selection handlers and the interaction with imported DXF geometry might require some familiarity with FreeCAD's Inventor/Coin3D integration and selection mechanisms.
19709.problem_summary: FreeCAD crashes with a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when a user clicks on a measurement label in the 3D viewer.
19709.root_cause_hypothesis: When the user clicks on a 3D measurement label, the selection event is handled by SoFCUnifiedSelection. The picked path resolves to an internal measurement Coin node (or an object without a standard document object / selection adapter), and SoFCUnifiedSelection attempts to dereference null or invalid object pointers/metadata when processing the picked element, accompanied by the log 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure'.
19709.suggested_approach: Add null checks and guard against picking non-selectable measurement scene graph nodes in SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection and SoFCUnifiedSelection::handleEvent, or ensure measurement label Coin nodes are explicitly marked non-pickable / non-selectable for standard document selection passes.
prerequisites: Build environment for FreeCAD with Coin3D, Qt, and Python bindings enabled.
A test DXF file or generic CAD model reproducing measurement creation in the Measure workbench.
implementation_steps: Reproduce the crash in a debug build by creating a measurement with the Measure tool and clicking directly on the resulting measurement label in the 3D viewport.

Inspect the stack frame in `Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection` and `handleEvent` to identify which pointer dereference or index lookup is causing the SIGSEGV when a measurement label node is picked.
Add null checks and valid-object validation in `SoFCUnifiedSelection` for picked paths that lack a backing `App::DocumentObject` or `Gui::ViewProvider`.
Check measurement Coin nodes (like text / dimension labels in `Mod/Measure`) and verify if their pick style should be set to `SoPickStyle::UNPICKABLE` or handled gracefully if selected.

Investigate and handle the warning 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure' to ensure measurement entities do not recursively attempt to measure themselves or fail silently without crashing.
Test clicking measurement labels across different geometry types (DXF 2D shapes, 3D solids, empty space) to confirm the crash is eliminated and selection behaves as expected.

28930.title: Measurement: Length measured with `Std_Measure` is attached to geometric center, not midpoint
28930.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies the problem and expected behavior in the measurement tool, but locating where the calculation uses the geometric center versus the curve midpoint requires navigating the C++ codebase of the Std_Measure tool.
28930.problem_summary: When measuring the length of a curved edge or spline with Std_Measure, the annotation label/dimension line anchor attaches to the geometric center (barycenter/bounding center) rather than the midpoint lying directly on the curve.
28930.root_cause_hypothesis: The measurement calculation for edge length queries the center of mass (e.g., via `BRepGProp` center of mass or bounding box center) or a similar centroid calculation instead of evaluating the point on the curve at parameter `(u_start + u_end) / 2` or at half of the edge's total arc length.
28930.suggested_approach: Update the point/placement calculation in the measurement code for edge length measurements to evaluate the point at the parametric midpoint or arc-length midpoint of the edge/curve using OpenCASCADE curve evaluation utilities (e.g. `BRepAdaptor_Curve` or `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), ensuring the annotation anchor sits directly on the curve.
prerequisites: Build FreeCAD from source with OpenCASCADE (OCC) development headers and Qt support enabled.
implementation_steps: Search the Measure module and Gui measurement commands for the calculation of the position/anchor point for length measurements of TopoDS_Edge and curve objects.
Identify where the barycenter or center of mass is currently computed (such as `GProp_GProps` / `BRepGProp::LinearProperties` or center point computation).

Modify the calculation for edge/curve length measurement to compute the curve's midpoint: retrieve the first and last curve parameters (or use arc length parameterization via `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), evaluate the 3D point at the midpoint parameter using OCC's `Value()` or `D0()` method.
Handle edge cases such as closed/periodic curves, zero-length edges, and trimmed curves properly.
Rebuild FreeCAD and verify using Std_Measure on various non-straight curves (splines, circles, arcs, ellipses, complex NURBS edges) to ensure annotations sit on the curve itself.
Run existing measurement unit and GUI tests to ensure no regressions for straight edge length or other measurement types.

21091.title: Link: On copy, don't preselect App::Link sources
21091.feasibility_reason: The issue requests changing the default behavior of the copy dialog for App::Link objects to not preselect link sources. While marked as a good first issue, navigating the FreeCAD copy/duplicate dialog logic and App::Link source selection code without prior codebase knowledge may take some investigation.
21091.problem_summary: When copying an App::Link object (or an assembly containing links), the copy/duplicate dependency selection dialog automatically preselects the linked source objects for copying, which duplicates the source objects instead of copying just the link that references the existing source.
21091.root_cause_hypothesis: The copy dependency resolution logic in FreeCAD (likely in Gui::Application, Dialog::DlgCheckableTree, or App::DocumentObject/App::LinkBaseExtension dependency traversal) includes outbound link target dependencies when gathering objects to be preselected in the copy dialog, without distinguishing between structural child objects and linked references.
21091.suggested_approach: Adjust the dependency gathering or pre-selection logic used during clipboard copy / duplicate dialog creation so that App::Link / App::LinkBase linked targets (or non-contained referenced objects) are excluded from the preselected objects by default, while keeping them visible or selectable in the dialog if needed.
prerequisites: Working FreeCAD development environment capable of building the GUI
Understanding of FreeCAD's document object dependency tree and App::Link architecture
implementation_steps: Locate the copy command implementation and the dialog creation (typically in Gui::Application::copy or Gui::Dialog::DlgCheckableTree / Gui::CommandDoc).
Trace where dependencies are collected and marked as checked/preselected before showing the copy dialog to the user.

Inspect how App::Link targets are retrieved, specifically checking whether the dependency is marked as a link reference (e.g. via isLinkSource, App::LinkBase::getLinkedObject, or PropertyLink / PropertyXLink).

Update the dependency collection or check state logic so that objects referenced purely via an App::Link / App::LinkBase reference are either excluded from the prechecked list or defaulted to unchecked.
Verify that the paste/duplicate logic properly preserves the reference to the original link source when the source itself is not copied.
Manually test copying an App::Link alone and an App::Part containing App::Links to ensure only the link/part is preselected and paste correctly points to the existing linked objects.
Add or update unit/GUI tests covering copying objects with links to ensure no regression.

32557.root_cause_hypothesis: The accelerator shortcut string defined for the Sketcher Scale command begins with an existing complete multi-key shortcut assigned to another command ('Z, P'), creating an unreachable prefix conflict in FreeCAD's shortcut handler.
32557.suggested_approach: Locate the command definition for Sketcher Scale (and related transform tools in Sketcher) and update the shortcut accelerator string so that it does not share an active prefix with another shortcut, ensuring all shortcuts in the group remain distinct and reachable.

Familiarity with FreeCAD's `DEF_STD_CMD_A` command macro and `sAccel` shortcut definition conventions

Inspect the existing shortcuts in the same tool group/toolbar to review for any other conflicting multi-key prefixes.
Update the shortcut string for the Scale command (e.g. to a distinct sequence that does not conflict with existing bindings, aligning with community/maintainer consensus on shortcut assignments).
Verify whether any documentation, tooltips, or tests reference the old shortcut string.
Compile FreeCAD and open the Sketcher workbench.
Test that pressing the shortcuts for both Rotate / Polar Transform and Scale triggers their respective tools without interference.

24440.title: PartDesign: UX could use optimization in order to add elements on some lists
24440.feasibility_reason: The issue requests UX improvements across multiple PartDesign tasks (Additive/Subtractive Pipe, profiles, sections) to match the selection behavior of Fillet/Chamfer and adding standard keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click) to lists. While straightforward Qt UI work, it touches multiple task panels and list widgets in the PartDesign workbench, requiring familiarity with FreeCAD's task panel architecture.
24440.problem_summary: PartDesign Pipe (and Loft) task panels have an inefficient workflow for adding/removing edges, sections, and auxiliary profiles: users must click the 'Add' button repeatedly for each element, and the list widgets lack standard multi-selection capabilities (Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click, Ctrl+A).
24440.root_cause_hypothesis: The selection handlers in TaskPipeParameters (and related Loft/Sweep panels) disconnect or exit the selection observer after a single sub-element pick instead of maintaining an active toggle/selection mode like Fillet/Chamfer panels. Additionally, the corresponding QListWidgets in the UI files default to single selection mode (QAbstractItemView::SingleSelection) rather than ExtendedSelection.
24440.suggested_approach: Update the Add/Remove buttons in TaskPipeParameters and TaskLoftParameters to act as toggle buttons that keep selection mode active until toggled off or another tool is selected (matching the behavior in TaskFilletParameters/TaskChamferParameters). Also configure the QListWidget instances to use ExtendedSelection mode to support Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click, and Ctrl+A for selecting multiple items.
prerequisites: A working FreeCAD build environment (C++20, Qt 5/6, CMake).
Basic familiarity with FreeCAD's Gui::SelectionObserver and PartDesign TaskPanel architecture.
implementation_steps: Examine TaskFilletParameters / TaskChamferParameters to observe how continuous edge selection and checkable add/remove toggle buttons are implemented with SelectionObserver.

Inspect TaskPipeParameters.ui and TaskLoftParameters.ui: update QListWidget selectionMode properties from SingleSelection to ExtendedSelection (or set them via code using setSelectionMode(QAbstractItemView::ExtendedSelection)).
Modify 'Add Edge', 'Remove Edge', 'Add Section', and 'Remove Section' push buttons to be checkable (setCheckable(true)) in the UI or constructors.

Update button click / toggle handlers in TaskPipeParameters.cpp and TaskLoftParameters.cpp to enter continuous selection mode while the button is checked, allowing the user to click multiple 3D elements sequentially without re-clicking the button.

Ensure that picking an element in 3D view adds/removes it from the list and model, but does not uncheck the button or detach the selection gate until the user explicitly toggles it off or finishes the task.
Update the list item deletion / remove logic so that when multiple list items are selected via Shift/Ctrl or Ctrl+A, clicking 'Remove' deletes all selected items at once.
Test Additive and Subtractive Pipe operations with single clicks, multiple consecutive 3D edge/section picks, and multi-selection list removals.
